captions.caption: A large fire burns dry grass and wood on a sandy beach.
The fire has subsided, leaving a pile of white ash and charred wood.
Close-up of the glowing embers and white ash from the fire.
The remains of the fire sit on the sand, still smoking slightly.
A person uses a long stick to poke at the center of the ash pile.
Two people use sticks to carefully lift a clay pot out of the hot ashes.
The clay pot is successfully lifted from the center of the extinguished fire.
The pot is moved away from the main pile of ash using the sticks.
A person sets the hot clay pot down on the sandy ground.
One person taps the side of the clay pot with a small stick.
The person continues to tap the pot, likely checking its integrity after firing.
A person carries a large, dark rock across the sand.
The person bends down to place the large rock on the sandy surface.
The first rock is firmly positioned in the sand.
A person walks towards a tree to pick up some dry branches.
The person carries a bundle of wood back towards the workspace.
The person sets the bundle of wood down on the sand near the rocks.
The person walks away from the wood pile to retrieve another item.
A person picks up a second large rock from the ground.
The person carries the second rock towards the first one.
The second rock is placed on the sand near the first rock.
The person adjusts the position of the second rock on the sand.
The person walks to get a third rock for the stove setup.
A person picks up a third large rock and brings it over.
The third rock is placed to complete a triangular base on the sand.
The person steps back to evaluate the placement of the three rocks.
Two people crouch down to adjust the rocks and clear the sand between them.
They use their hands to dig slightly into the sand around the rocks.
The rocks are being firmly embedded into the sand to create a stable base.
The people continue to level the sand and position the three stones.
A person checks the stability of the rock formation.
One person reaches for the fired clay pot nearby.
The person carefully places the clay pot on top of the three rocks.
The pot is adjusted so it sits level on the stone tripod.
Both people work together to ensure the pot is secure on the rocks.
They push sand around the base of the rocks for extra stability.
Final adjustments are made to the clay pot's position on the stove.
The pot is now sitting ready on the primitive stone stove.
A person walks away from the stove towards the ocean.
The person walks into the shallow seawater carrying a small container.
He continues walking further into the water to reach a cleaner spot.
The person stops in the water and prepares to submerge the container.
He bends down and dips the small clay pot into the seawater.
The container is filled with seawater from the ocean.
The person stands up, carrying the container full of water.
He begins walking back towards the shore and the campfire site.
The person walks out of the water and across the sand.
He approaches the other person sitting by the rock stove.
The person starts pouring the seawater into the large clay pot.
Seawater flows from the smaller container into the larger pot on the stove.
He continues pouring until the smaller container is empty.
The person finishes pouring and sets the smaller container down.
One person holds a clay lid while the other prepares to fetch more water.
A close-up shows the clay pot sitting on the rocks with a lid nearby.
A person picks up the lid and places it on top of the clay pot.
The lid is removed again as the other person returns with more water.
The person begins pouring another container of seawater into the pot.
More seawater is added to the large clay pot on the stone stove.
The person continues pouring the water carefully into the opening.
The second container of seawater is emptied into the large pot.
